A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiffusionBlocks work. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, figures and tables, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, image-generation and language-modeling experiments in Tables 1–5, alongside original ablation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds Tiny-ImageNet classification, ImageNet block-count results and ViT timing measurements.

M1.justification: The network conversion, independent denoising objectives, equi-probability partitioning and architecture adaptations remain unchanged. Appendix C newly documents embedding L2 normalization, but the PDFs do not establish that this represents a changed procedure rather than an implementation detail previously omitted.

E1.justification: Appendix F.1 adds classification on Tiny-ImageNet, covering 200 classes and 64×64 images. All earlier datasets and tasks remain. The additional ImageNet block-count configurations and training-reference FID evaluations extend settings within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in matched experiments, including Forward-Forward in Table 1 and Backprop plus NoProp-DT/CT/FM in Table 6. The new classification and timing comparisons use the existing ViT baseline. Appendix G discusses activation checkpointing analytically without adding an evaluated checkpointing baseline.

E3.justification: The reported CIFAR-100 learning rate changes from 0.001 to 0.0005, and ImageNet batch size from 1024 to 512. FID evaluation expands from test references to both training and test references. New protocols cover Tiny-ImageNet, the 24-layer ImageNet block-count sweep and ViT timing. These substantially extend evaluation settings; the revised descriptions alone do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v3 extends the existing block-count sensitivity study to ImageNet in Table 8 and adds a limited ViT timing analysis in Appendix H. Earlier partitioning and block-count analyses remain: v2 Tables 8 and 9 become v3 Tables 10 and 11. These are targeted additions to the existing analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix H newly specifies averaging wall-time measurements over 100 iterations. Both versions retain minimum-of-three FID reporting. No training-seed counts, confidence intervals or variability estimates are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ViT/Forward-Forward/DiffusionBlocks accuracy from 45.26/15.77/45.46 to 60.25/7.85/59.30, reversing the ViT–DiffusionBlocks ordering under revised reported settings. Table 2 retains test FIDs and adds training-reference FIDs: 32.84/30.59 for CIFAR-10 and 9.01/9.00 for ImageNet, ordered baseline/DiffusionBlocks. New results include ImageNet block-count FIDs, Tiny-ImageNet accuracy of 35.32 versus 36.16, and timing of 0.0507 seconds for ViT versus 0.0181 per block and a calculated 0.0543 aggregate for DiffusionBlocks.

T1.justification: Appendices G–H add memory and computation derivations, including Adam-state memory accounting, checkpointing's approximate 4/3 computation overhead and equal aggregate layer-evaluation counts for block training. The original diffusion equations and masked-diffusion derivation remain unchanged; the notation appendix mainly restates existing definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract's scientific claims and the introduction's four contributions retain their meaning: independent diffusion-based block training, balanced partitioning, broad applicability and memory/computation benefits. Added experiments support these claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: The conclusion adds partition granularity as an open question and refines the proposed performance mechanisms into direct target supervision and noise-range specialization. Appendix C explains embedding collapse, while Appendices G–H distinguish memory savings from aggregate training computation and discuss compatibility with checkpointing. Existing architectural and scaling limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands reproducibility information: a project code-access link, embedding normalization, ViT patch size, augmentation and scheduling, ImageNet training duration and guidance scale, and ADM/clean-fid evaluation implementations. It also supplies Tiny-ImageNet hyperparameters and H100 timing hardware details. Table 6 newly clarifies that comparator scores were taken from NoProp. These disclosures do not themselves establish implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for RandAugment, ADM, classifier-free guidance, Tiny-ImageNet and clean-fid, and removes Neyshabur (2017). Section 4 largely preserves the positioning against block-wise and stage-specific diffusion methods; Appendix G adds a focused comparison with activation checkpointing.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section order remain. v3 clarifies input/target notation, distinguishes the noise-sampling distribution, expands the conclusion, reorganizes appendices and adds author contributions and acknowledgements. Editing is localized, with some new defects, including the malformed configuration sentence in Section 5.6.2.

P2.justification: v3 adds a notation table and ImageNet, Tiny-ImageNet and timing result tables. Table 2 displays train/test FID pairs, the NoProp comparison becomes a standalone display, and the CIFAR-10 block-count table moves into the appendix. All six figures are retained, with limited caption, notation and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: Additional benchmark and sensitivity results strengthen validation, while implementation disclosures and code-access information improve reproducibility. Table 12 usefully separates measured per-block time from calculated aggregate training cost. These targeted gains outweigh limited documentation problems, including Appendix H's three-step inference example conflicting with the four steps retained in Appendix E.1. The changed classification scores accompany revised settings and do not establish a same-setting performance improvement.
